terms.context: - $\alpha$ is the **Startup Latency**\index{LogGP model!startup latency} (seconds)---the fixed cost of initiating a message, including software overhead, NIC processing, and routing setup
- $\beta$ is the **Link Bandwidth**\index{LogGP model!link bandwidth} (bytes/s)---the sustained data rate after startup
The **Crossover Message Size**\index{LogGP model!crossover message size} $n^*$, defined by @eq-crossover, is the point where both terms contribute equally:

Below $n^*$, communication is **Latency-Dominated**\index{Latency-dominated communication}: sending more small messages wastes time on repeated startups. Above $n^*$, communication is **Bandwidth-Dominated**\index{Bandwidth-dominated communication}: the link is fully utilized, and the only way to go faster is higher bandwidth.

Above $n^*$, communication is **Bandwidth-Dominated**\index{Bandwidth-dominated communication}: the link is fully utilized, and the only way to go faster is higher bandwidth.

The $\alpha$-$\beta$ model assumes a message is a single, atomic transfer. In practice, networks pipeline messages: a sender can inject a new packet before the previous one has been fully received. Collective operations move data between all $N$ GPUs simultaneously. Each collective has a characteristic bandwidth term (how much data flows) and latency term (how many sequential message steps are required). The formulas below use the **Bandwidth-Optimal Ring Algorithm**\index{Ring algorithm!bandwidth optimal} unless otherwise noted; @sec-appdx-comm-foundations-algorithm-selection discusses when other algorithms are preferable.

terms.canonical_expansion: primitive in Fully Sharded Data Parallelism
terms.context: AllGather is the complement of ReduceScatter: each GPU starts with a $M/N$-sized shard and ends with the complete $M$-byte tensor. It is the core communication primitive in Fully Sharded Data Parallelism (FSDP) for reconstructing parameters before each forward pass, and in tensor parallelism for reassembling split activations.

terms.canonical_expansion: is the routing primitive for Mixture-of-Experts
terms.context: AllToAll is the most general collective: each GPU sends a distinct $M/N$-sized chunk to every other GPU, and receives a distinct chunk from each. It is the routing primitive for Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architectures, where tokens must be dispatched to the correct expert and the results gathered back.

Pipeline parallelism splits a model across multiple GPUs so that each GPU holds only a fraction of the layers. The trade-off is **Bubble Time**\index{Pipeline!bubble time}: idle cycles where GPUs wait for activations or gradients from upstream or downstream stages. Quantifying the bubble fraction reveals whether pipeline parallelism is worth the complexity at a given scale.
